reading.title: Don't throw it away — fix it!
text: What do you do when your toaster stops working or your favourite jeans get a hole? Most people simply throw them away and buy new ones. But in towns around the world, more and more people are taking their broken things to a repair café instead.

The first repair café opened in Amsterdam in 2009. The idea came from Martine Postma, a journalist who was worried about how much people were throwing away. Today there are more than 2,500 repair cafés in over 40 countries. Most of them meet once a month in a library, a church hall or a community centre.

It works like this. Visitors bring a broken item, and volunteers with useful skills, such as electricians, tailors and bike mechanics, help them to repair it. The repairs are free, although most cafés ask for a small donation. While they wait, visitors can have a cup of tea and chat with their neighbours.

The volunteers don't just fix things for people — they fix things with them. 'I want visitors to watch and learn,' says Peter Hollis, a retired engineer who helps at a café in Bristol. 'Next time, they might be able to do it themselves.' About 60% of the items are repaired successfully. The most common ones are lamps, coffee machines, clothes and bicycles.

Supporters say repair cafés are good for the environment because fewer things end up in rubbish dumps. But for many visitors, the social side is just as important. As one regular visitor says, 'I came to fix a radio, but I stayed because of the people.'

reading.title: One month, no shopping: what I learned
text: I used to be the kind of person who bought something almost every day. Nothing expensive — a coffee, a phone case, a T-shirt on offer. But in January, when I checked my bank statement, I was shocked. I had spent nearly £400 on things I didn't really need. So I decided to try a challenge: for the whole of February, I would buy nothing except food, medicine and bus tickets.

The first week was the hardest. I get lots of emails from online shops, and every time I saw 'Everything half price — today only!', I wanted to click. So I unsubscribed from almost all of them. I also stopped going to the shops at lunchtime and took a packed lunch to work, which I usually ate in the park with a colleague.

By the second week, I noticed some changes. I was spending more time with things I already had. I finally read three books that I had bought the year before, and I cooked meals with whatever was in the cupboard. When my headphones broke, I didn't buy new ones. My brother lent me his old pair instead.

Not everything was easy. It was my friend Leo's birthday, and I couldn't buy him a present. I felt a bit embarrassed, so I made him a card and baked his favourite chocolate cake. He said it was the best present he got that year, which was really kind of him.

At the end of the month, I had saved £320. I've put most of it into a savings account for a trip to Portugal this summer. Will I do it again? Probably not for a whole month, but I've changed some of my habits. Now I wait 48 hours before I buy anything that isn't essential. If I still want it after two days, I buy it. Most of the time, I don't.

listening.title: Getting fit
listening.context: Maria asks her friend Ben for advice because she wants to join a gym.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Ben, can I ask you something? I'm thinking of joining a gym. You go to one, don't you?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I used to, but I stopped last year. It was too expensive, and I got bored of the machines.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Oh, really? How much was it?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Thirty-five pounds a month. And I only went about twice a week, so it wasn't worth it.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Hmm. The one near my office is forty pounds, but it opens at six in the morning, so I could go before work.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Are you really going to get up at half past five? You hate mornings!

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Well, that's true. I'm not very good at getting up early. So what do you do now?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I've joined a running club. It's free, and we meet in Riverside Park on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at seven.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Free? That's amazing. But I'm not fit enough. I can't run for more than ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Don't worry, there's a beginners' group. They run and walk for the first few weeks. Lots of people start that way.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: OK, that sounds less scary. Is there a session this Thursday?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes. If you like, I'll meet you at the park gate at quarter to seven and introduce you to the coach.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Great, let's do that. And if I don't like it, I can still join the gym.

listening.title: Car-Free Day
listening.context: A presenter on a local radio station gives information about an event this weekend.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and here's some news for people in Westfield. This Sunday is our town's third Car-Free Day.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: From nine in the morning until six in the evening, the town centre will be closed to cars, so please don't try to drive into town.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: Getting there is easy, though. All buses are free on Sunday, and they'll run every ten minutes instead of every twenty.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: There's lots to do. The main street is turned into a big market, with food stalls, live music and games for children.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: There's also a free cycling lesson for adults who never learned to ride a bike. It starts at eleven outside the library, and you don't need to book. Just turn up.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: The event is organised by the town council, and last year it was visited by more than twenty thousand people.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: The forecast looks good: sunny, but a bit windy in the afternoon, so you might want to bring a jacket.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: For a map of the closed roads, have a look at the council's website. Enjoy your Sunday!

writing.prompt: Your English-speaking friend Sam is visiting your city for a weekend next month and has asked for your advice. Write an email to Sam (120–160 words). Suggest places to visit, food Sam should try, the best way to get around, and what to bring.
writing.promptMn: Англиар ярьдаг найз Сэм тань ирэх сард таны хотод амралтын өдрүүдээр зочлохоор ирэх гэж байгаа бөгөөд танаас зөвлөгөө хүссэн байна. Сэмд имэйл бичээрэй (120–160 үг): үзэх газрууд, заавал амсаж үзэх хоол, хотоор зорчих хамгийн тохиромжтой арга, юу авч ирэх талаар зөвлөөрэй.
points: A friendly opening that reacts to Sam's news
Two places to visit and why (comparatives and superlatives)
Food Sam should try (should / have to)
The best way to get around
What to bring (first conditional: If it's cold, …)
A friendly ending with a plan (future forms)
writing.sample:
Hi Sam,

It's great to hear that you're coming to Ulaanbaatar next month! I can't wait to see you.

On Saturday morning you should definitely visit Gandan Monastery. It's one of the most beautiful places in the city, and it's much quieter before lunch. After that, we could go to the National Museum, which is the best place to learn about Mongolian history.

You have to try buuz and khuushuur while you're here. If you like meat, you'll love them! I know a small restaurant near my flat that isn't too expensive.

Getting around is easy. Buses are cheap, but taxis are more comfortable, especially late in the evening.

One more thing: October can be really cold here, so bring a warm coat and a hat.

Let me know when your flight arrives, and I'll meet you at the airport.

See you soon,
Bat

speaking.prompt: Would you prefer to live in a big city or in a small town? Give your opinion with reasons and examples from your own life, and say what you would change about the place where you live now if you could.
speaking.promptMn: Та том хотод эсвэл жижиг хотод амьдрахыг илүүд үзэх үү? Өөрийн амьдралаас жишээ татаж, шалтгаанаа тайлбарлан санал бодлоо хэлээрэй. Мөн боломж байсан бол одоо амьдарч буй газартаа юуг өөрчлөхийг хүсэхээ хэлээрэй.
points: Your preference and the main reason
An example from your own experience (past simple)
What you would change if you could (second conditional)
phrases: If I could change one thing, I'd…
speaking.sample: I live in Ulaanbaatar, the biggest city in Mongolia, but to be honest, I'd prefer to live in a smaller town. The main reason is the traffic. The city is much more crowded than it used to be, and it sometimes takes me an hour to get to work. Air pollution is also a big problem in winter. On the other hand, big cities have a lot of advantages. There are more jobs, better hospitals and more things to do in your free time. For example, last weekend I went to a concert and then tried a new restaurant — you can't do that in a small village. So for me, the best choice is a peaceful town that isn't too far from a big city. If I could change one thing about Ulaanbaatar, I'd improve public transport. If there were more buses and a metro, fewer people would drive, and the air would be much cleaner.

questions.prompt: Mmm, this soup ___ delicious! What's in it?
questions.explanation: Here 'taste' describes the soup, so it is a state verb: use the present simple, not the present continuous.
questions.explanationMn: Энд 'taste' нь шөлний амтыг тодорхойлж буй төлөвийн үйл үг тул энгийн одоо цаг (tastes) хэрэглэнэ, үргэлжилсэн цаг хэрэглэхгүй.

questions.prompt: Someone knocked at the door while I ___ (watch) TV.
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous for a longer action in progress (watching TV) that a shorter action (knocked) interrupted.
questions.explanationMn: Богино үйлдлээр (knocked) тасалдсан, тухайн үед үргэлжилж байсан урт үйлдлийг өнгөрсөн үргэлжилсэн цагаар (was watching) илэрхийлнэ.

answers: I used to play football every weekend.
As a child, I used to play football every weekend.
I used to play football every weekend as a child.

As a child, I used to play football every weekend, but I don't now.
questions.explanation: 'Used to + infinitive' describes a past habit that is not true any more.
questions.explanationMn: 'Used to + үйл үг' нь одоо байхгүй болсон, өнгөрсөн үеийн зуршлыг илэрхийлнэ.

questions.prompt: Tap the part of the sentence with the mistake.
questions.explanation: Don't use 'more' with a one-syllable adjective: cheap → cheaper.
questions.explanationMn: Нэг үетэй тэмдэг нэрийн өмнө 'more' хэрэглэхгүй: cheap → cheaper.

questions.prompt: There ___ chairs for everyone — we need five more.
questions.explanation: 'Chairs' is a plural countable noun, so use 'aren't enough' (not enough = fewer than we need).
questions.explanationMn: 'Chairs' тоологдох, олон тоотой нэр үг тул 'aren't enough' (хангалттай биш) гэнэ.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same. Use the word given.
questions.sentence: I started working at this company three years ago, and I still work here.
answers: I have worked at this company for three years.
I have been working at this company for three years.
I have worked here for three years.
I have been working here for three years.
I have been at this company for three years.
questions.explanation: Use the present perfect with 'for' + a period of time for something that started in the past and continues now.
questions.explanationMn: Өнгөрсөнд эхлээд одоо ч үргэлжилж байгаа зүйлд одоо төгссөн цаг + 'for' + хугацаа хэрэглэнэ.

questions.prompt: Correct the mistake in the sentence.
questions.sentence: I haven't finished my homework already.
answers: I haven't finished my homework yet.
I have not finished my homework yet.
questions.explanation: Use 'yet' in negative sentences and questions. 'Already' is for things that happened sooner than expected.
questions.explanationMn: Үгүйсгэх болон асуух өгүүлбэрт 'yet' хэрэглэнэ. 'Already' нь хүлээж байснаас эрт болсон зүйлд хэрэглэгдэнэ.

questions.prompt: If you practise every day, you ___ speak much more fluently by the summer.
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + infinitive. 'Can' has no future form, so use 'will be able to'.
questions.explanationMn: Нэгдүгээр нөхцөлт өгүүлбэр: if + энгийн одоо цаг, will + үйл үг. 'Can' ирээдүй цагийн хэлбэргүй тул 'will be able to' хэрэглэнэ.

questions.prompt: Would you mind ___ the window? It's a bit cold in here.
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is a polite request and is followed by the -ing form.
questions.explanationMn: 'Would you mind' нь эелдэг хүсэлт бөгөөд араасаа үйл үгийн -ing хэлбэр авна.

questions.prompt: I was ___ that I fell asleep in the middle of the film.
questions.explanation: 'Bored' describes how a person feels ('boring' describes the film). Use 'so' + adjective; 'such' needs a noun (such a boring film).
questions.explanationMn: 'Bored' нь хүний мэдрэмжийг, 'boring' нь тухайн зүйлийг тодорхойлно. Дан тэмдэг нэрийн өмнө 'so', нэр үгтэй бол 'such' хэрэглэнэ (such a boring film).

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same. Use the word given.
questions.sentence: I don't have enough money, so I can't buy a new car.
answers: If I had enough money, I would buy a new car.
I would buy a new car if I had enough money.
If I had enough money, I would be able to buy a new car.
I would be able to buy a new car if I had enough money.
questions.explanation: Second conditional for an unreal present situation: if + past simple, would + infinitive.
questions.explanationMn: Одоогийн бодит бус нөхцөлийг хоёрдугаар нөхцөлт өгүүлбэрээр илэрхийлнэ: if + өнгөрсөн энгийн цаг, would + үйл үг.

questions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
questions.answer: The bridge which was built in 1890 is still used today.
alternatives: The bridge which is still used today was built in 1890.
questions.explanation: Use 'which' (or 'that') for things, not 'who'. Use the passive ('was built', 'is used') because we don't say who built or uses it.
questions.explanationMn: Юмсын хувьд 'who' биш 'which' (эсвэл 'that') хэрэглэнэ. Хэн барьсан, хэн ашигладаг нь чухал биш тул идэвхгүй хэв (was built, is used) хэрэглэнэ.

questions.prompt: My grandfather never gets angry, even when he has to wait for a long time. He's very ___.
questions.explanation: A patient person can wait calmly without getting angry.
questions.explanationMn: Patient — тэвчээртэй; уурлалгүй, тайван хүлээж чаддаг хүн.

questions.prompt: I live in a quiet ___ about twenty minutes from the city centre.
questions.explanation: A neighbourhood is an area of a town or city where people live.
questions.explanationMn: Neighbourhood — хотын нэг хэсэг, хүмүүсийн амьдардаг хороолол.

questions.prompt: The doctor told me to ___ more exercise and eat less sugar.

questions.prompt: Our flight was ___ by three hours because of heavy snow, so we had a long wait at the airport.
